item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
This figure will be turned to a different position.

[Image: A 3D figure made of cubes]

Which of these could be the figure after it is turned?
item.figure_description: The initial figure is a solid composed of 5 cubes: 4 cubes form an upright T-shape (a horizontal row of 3 cubes at the bottom, and 1 cube centered on top of the middle cube), and a 5th cube is attached to the back face of the leftmost cube of the bottom row. Option A shows an upside-down T-shape (a horizontal row of 3 cubes at the top with 1 cube centered below the middle cube) with a 5th cube attached to the back face of the rightmost cube. Option B shows an upright T-shape with a 5th cube attached to the back face of the rightmost cube. Option C shows an upright T-shape with a 5th cube attached to the front face of the middle bottom cube. Option D shows a vertical column of 3 cubes with 2 cubes extending to the right and backward from the middle cube.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: 3-D figure]

Which of these could be folded to make a shape like the 3-D figure above?
reference_items.figure_description:
At the top, a perspective drawing of a right triangular prism lying horizontally on one rectangular face. The front and back faces are triangles, connected by three rectangular faces.

Below are four candidate nets labeled A, B, C, and D:
- A: A chain consisting of a rectangle at an angle, a triangle, a central horizontal rectangle, a triangle, and another rectangle angled upward.
- B: Three identical horizontal rectangles stacked vertically, with two triangles attached to the right edge of the top two rectangles, pointing to the right.
- C: Two horizontal rectangles stacked vertically with two triangles attached to their left side pointing left, and a third rectangle extending to the right with a triangle attached at its right end.
- D: Three identical horizontal rectangles stacked vertically in a column; one triangle is attached to the right side of the top rectangle pointing right, and another triangle is attached to the left side of the bottom rectangle pointing left.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A shaded geometric shape]

The shape above is rotated by 90° clockwise. Which shape is the result?
reference_items.figure_description:
At the top, a shaded grey shape formed by two perpendicular arms meeting at a top-left corner: a longer vertical arm extending downwards and a shorter horizontal arm extending to the right. A small vertical oval cutout/hole is positioned near the right end of the top horizontal arm.

Below are four multiple-choice options:
- Option A: A shaded grey shape with a corner at the bottom-left; a long vertical arm extends upwards and a shorter horizontal arm extends to the right along the bottom. A vertical oval hole is near the right end of the bottom horizontal arm.
- Option B: A shaded grey shape with a corner at the top-right; a shorter horizontal arm extends to the left along the top and a longer vertical arm extends downwards on the right. A vertical oval hole is near the left end of the top horizontal arm.
- Option C: A shaded grey shape with a corner at the top-right; a longer horizontal arm extends to the left along the top and a shorter vertical arm extends downwards on the right. A horizontal oval hole is near the bottom end of the vertical arm.
- Option D: A shaded grey shape with a corner at the bottom-right; a shorter horizontal arm extends to the left along the bottom and a longer vertical arm extends upwards on the right. A vertical oval hole is near the left end of the bottom horizontal arm.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Ariana found the following patterns to make containers. Which pattern actually makes the container shown beside it?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: a pattern made up by squares and a cube to the right of the pattern]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: a pattern made up by two circles on the ends of a rectangular shape and a cylinder to the right of the pattern]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: a pattern made up by square and two triangles coming out of two sides of the square and a square base pyramid to the right of the pattern]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: a pattern made up by two large rectangles and four small rectangles with two of the smaller rectangles coming out of the opposite shorter sides of the large rectangles and a rectangular prism]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four multiple-choice options, each showing a 2D net (with dashed interior fold lines) beside a 3D container (with dashed hidden edges):
- Option A: A net of 5 congruent squares arranged in an inverted U-shape (a row of 3 squares across the top, and 1 square hanging down from each of the left and right squares, leaving the middle space empty). Beside it is a line drawing of a cube.
- Option B: A net consisting of a horizontal rectangle with a circle attached to each of its two shorter vertical ends. Beside it is a line drawing of a vertical cylinder.
- Option C: A net consisting of a square with two triangles attached to adjacent sides: one extending down from the bottom side and one extending to the right from the right side. Beside it is a line drawing of an inverted square-based pyramid pointing downward.
- Option D: A net consisting of a horizontal row of four rectangles alternating in width (narrow, wide, narrow, wide), with a narrow rectangle attached to the top of the first wide rectangle and a narrow rectangle attached to the bottom of the second wide rectangle. Beside it is a line drawing of a matching upright rectangular prism.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Geometry Tiles
Instruction:

For this item, you have been given a piece of cardboard with 6 tiles like the ones shown below. Take the piece of cardboard, and punch out the 6 tiles.

If you do not have the piece of cardboard, raise your hand.

4 Triangle Tiles
[Image: Four triangle tiles]

2 Trapezoid Tiles
[Image: Two trapezoid tiles]

These tiles can be used to make new figures. One problem has been done for you

USE: 3 Triangle Tiles
MAKE: A trapezoid
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.
[Image: Example showing a trapezoid drawn on the grid]

Now try these problems.

C.

USE: 2 Trapezoid Tiles
MAKE: A 6-sided figure that is not the same shape as the one you made in Part B
SHOW: Draw it on the grid.

[Image: Triangular grid]

descriptors: Any of four figures (6-sided) that was not used in part B.
Repeats a correct figure already given in part B
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem includes four diagrams:
1. '4 Triangle Tiles': Four identical equilateral triangles of unit side length, arranged in a row pointing alternately up, down, up, and down.
2. '2 Trapezoid Tiles': Two identical isosceles trapezoids each composed of three equilateral triangle units (bottom base 2 units, top base 1 unit, legs 1 unit for the first one; and inverted with top base 2 units, bottom base 1 unit for the second one).
3. Worked example grid: An isometric grid forming a parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides of 3 units each and slanted sides of 2 units each, divided by dashed lines into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangles. In the top-right portion, a trapezoid made of 3 triangle units (top side 1 unit, bottom side 2 units, slanted sides 1 unit) is outlined in bold solid lines.
4. Part C response grid: An identical empty parallelogram-shaped isometric grid with top and bottom edges of 3 units, slanted sides of 2 units, divided into 2 rows of 6 equilateral triangle units by dashed lines.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A pattern rule says “Rotate the shape [Image: a circle with a dot in the middle connected by a straight line to the arc pointing up] 1/4 turn clockwise each time.”
What will the pattern look like?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: First circle pointing up, second circle pointing right, third circle pointing down, fourth circle pointing left.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: First circle pointing up, second circle pointing down, third circle pointing up, fourth circle pointing down.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: First circle pointing up, second circle pointing left, third circle pointing down, fourth circle pointing right.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: First circle pointing up, second circle pointing right, third circle pointing left, fourth circle pointing down.]

reference_items.figure_description:
In the stem, a circle has a central dot with a line segment extending straight up to the top edge (12 o'clock position).

Four response options each show a row of four circles showing different orientations of the line segment:
- Option A: First circle points straight up (12 o'clock); second points right (3 o'clock); third points straight down (6 o'clock); fourth points left (9 o'clock).
- Option B: First circle points straight up (12 o'clock); second points straight down (6 o'clock); third points straight up (12 o'clock); fourth points straight down (6 o'clock).
- Option C: First circle points straight up (12 o'clock); second points left (9 o'clock); third points straight down (6 o'clock); fourth points right (3 o'clock).
- Option D: First circle points straight up (12 o'clock); second points right (3 o'clock); third points left (9 o'clock); fourth points straight down (6 o'clock).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: six pieces of cardboard with length of the sides labeled in cm. Two of the pieces are square shaped with each side measured at 1 cm. Four of the pieces are rectangular shaped with two sides measured at 1 cm and two other sides measured at 2 cm.]

Susan has the 6 pieces of cardboard shown above. Which of the following shapes could Susan make using all 6 of these pieces without cutting them?
reference_items.figure_description:
At the top of the item, six gray-shaded flat cardboard shapes are shown. Two are identical squares, each labeled '1 cm' on all four sides (top, bottom, left, and right). Four are identical horizontal rectangles, each labeled '2 cm' on the top and bottom sides and '1 cm' on the left and right sides.

The response options show line drawings of four 3D geometric solids with dashed lines representing hidden edges:
- Option A: A cube.
- Option B: A triangular prism resting on one of its rectangular faces.
- Option C: A truncated pyramid with a square or rectangular base and top.
- Option D: A tall right rectangular prism standing on a square base.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

descriptors: Only 20, 30, 50 correctly entered on the scale.

reference_items.figure_description:
The item contains two images:
1. At the top, a circular spinner divided into three sectors: a large dark-grey sector spanning roughly half the circle (bottom-left), a medium grey sector (top-left, spanning roughly one-quarter), and a white sector (right side). An arrow is pivoted at the center pointing toward the upper-right into the white sector.
2. At the bottom, a vertical bar graph titled "Bar graph". The horizontal axis has tick marks labeled "Red", "Blue", and "Green" under three unfilled vertical rectangular bars: the "Red" bar is the tallest (5 grid units high), the "Blue" bar is 3 grid units high, and the "Green" bar is 2 grid units high. The vertical axis on the left has 6 tick marks connected to square answer boxes: the lowest tick mark at the baseline contains a box with the number "0" inside, and above it are 5 empty square boxes aligned with tick marks at heights 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 (matching the tops of the bars at 2, 3, and 5).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

Choose the value closest to it.
